blindSourceSummaries: A legal-aid organisation's report (13-28 March 2024): a regional court in this country placed a foreign trans woman (taking hormones since 2018) in a guarded detention centre for male foreigners; the border police refused to move her or to deliver her medication, interrupting her hormone therapy for three months; she was released after the NGO's application citing health grounds under the foreign-national statute's health provisions.

A trans-rights organisation report (16 July 2024): on 11 July an international human-rights court held that the national prison authorities violated the right to private and family life by denying a trans woman access to hormone replacement therapy while imprisoned (she had been prescribed hormones for almost two years; the prison gave no reasonable grounds for refusal); damages of about 8,000 in local currency ordered; the organisation had intervened as a third party in 2021; part of a growing international standard on trans prisoners' healthcare.
